segments.narration: Fifty-five oak posts rose out of a Norfolk beach. The tide had been peeling them free for years before anyone noticed.
In 1998 John Lorimer spotted a Bronze Age axe head in the silt. Then a circle appeared, six metres wide, closely fitted.
At its centre was an upturned oak stump, roots in the air, over a tonne of it. What was it for?
Tree rings dated every timber to a single felling, spring 2049 BC. One post had a narrow forked gap, the only way in.
That tight ring and single entrance point to a mortuary enclosure, where a body was laid out to the sky. The stump was the platform.
